doc.title: Charles Lloyd — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The wolf ticket and I don't do business
summary: Newton says Lloyd, like his grandfather, refused the wolf ticket; Lloyd says he has no checkbook or smartphone and does no business.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: But your grandfather was also a runaway. He wouldn’t accept the wolf ticket that was presented to African Americans during that time. He wouldn’t accept it. And you know what? You have not accepted it either. You’ve fought it your whole life, you know.
And you had another reality in your head, you know. Not only in your music, but in the way that you approach business, because there’s so few people.
I’ll tell you something interesting about business.
I don’t do no business. I don’t have no check book. I don’t have no smart phone. I don’t do no business.
